title: From Fighter Jets to Bobsleds: Utah Aerospace Leaders Team Up to Give USA Bobsled a Competitive Edge
summary: Leading the industry in advanced composite materials. Discover innovative, high-performance solutions for aerospace and more.
body_markdown:
Utah’s advanced technology ecosystem brings aerospace, composites and elite sport together ahead of the 2034 Olympic Winter Games


SALT LAKE CITY, UT (Oct. 28, 2026) — 47G, USA Bobsled & Skeleton (USABS), Albany Engineered Composites, Hexcel and Nammo Composite Solutions today announced a new partnership bringing together advanced materials, engineering and manufacturing expertise to support the development of the next generation of Team USA bobsleds. The partnership was announced at 47G’s annual Zero Gravity Summit, held as part of Hard Tech Week in Salt Lake City.


The collaboration brings together athletes, engineers, manufacturers and innovators to explore how technologies developed for some of the world’s most demanding applications can be applied to elite sport. The partnership also showcases the depth of Utah’s hard-tech ecosystem, connecting companies with expertise spanning aerospace, advanced materials, manufacturing and defense with athletes preparing to compete on the world’s biggest stage: The 2034 Winter Olympics.


“Partnerships like this are a great reminder that innovation can come from unexpected places,” said Lyndon Smith, President, Americas & Global Fibers. “The same advanced materials and technical expertise that support aerospace and defense can open new possibilities in elite sport. We’re excited to work alongside USA Bobsled & Skeleton and our industry partners to see what we can accomplish together.”


At the heart of the effort is the application of advanced composite technology to one of the most equipment-driven sports in the world. For USABS athletes, performance is measured in hundredths of a second, making the weight, strength, aerodynamics and design of a sled critical considerations on the track. As part of this partnership, Albany will work with USABS to design and manufacture next-generation composite bobsleds intended to support Team USA athletes through the 2034 and 2038 Winter Olympic Games. Hexcel is contributing advanced composite materials expertise, while Nammo Composite Solutions will design and manufacture carbon-fiber cowlings for Team USA’s two-man bobsleds.


The technology behind the partnership has applications far beyond the bobsled track. Advanced composite materials offer a combination of strength, durability and low weight that has made them essential to modern aerospace and defense applications, including aircraft, missiles and


unmanned systems. Albany, Hexcel and Nammo bring decades of experience engineering and manufacturing composite components for some of the world’s most demanding environments, and the USABS partnership creates an opportunity to apply that expertise to elite athletics. Together, these Utah-based companies are bringing aerospace and defense expertise in advanced materials and manufacturing to the development of high-performance sled technology.


“Advanced composite technology has helped transform aerospace by enabling engineers to design components that are strong, lightweight and capable of performing in some of the most demanding environments,” said Jeff Daniel, vice president, commercial segment at Albany Engineered Composites. “Bringing that expertise to bobsled creates an exciting opportunity to apply what we have learned in aerospace to a completely different performance challenge. We are proud to work alongside USA Bobsled & Skeleton to develop technology that can support Team USA athletes on the road to 2034 and beyond.”


The partnership comes as Utah prepares to welcome the Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games in 2034. USABS athletes already train and compete at Utah Olympic Park in Park City, creating a natural connection between the state’s technology ecosystem and the future of Team USA competition on home ice. For 47G, the collaboration represents an opportunity to demonstrate that Utah’s Olympic legacy can extend beyond hosting world-class competition. With advanced manufacturing, aerospace, defense, research and technology companies operating across the state, Utah has developed an ecosystem capable of bringing together expertise from traditionally separate industries.


“Utah has spent decades building an ecosystem where advanced manufacturing, aerospace, research and entrepreneurship intersect,” said Starks. “As we look toward 2034, we have an opportunity not only to host the world’s best athletes, but also to showcase the technologies, companies and talent helping shape the future of performance and innovation.”


The partnership was announced October 28 at 47G’s annual Zero Gravity Summit at the Salt Palace in Salt Lake City, held as part of Hard Tech Week. As Team USA prepares for the 2034 Winter Olympics on home ice, aerospace and advanced manufacturing expertise is finding a new proving ground on the bobsled track. ###

About USA Bobsled & Skeleton USA Bobsled & Skeleton (USABS) is the national governing body for bobsled and skeleton in the United States. USABS promotes and grows the sports while recruiting, developing, training and supporting athletes from their introduction to bobsled and skeleton through elite international competition.


About Albany Engineered Composites Albany Engineered Composites, a segment of Albany International Corp. (NYSE: AIN), designs and manufactures advanced engineered composite components for demanding applications in commercial and military aircraft, missiles and unmanned vehicles. Albany Engineered Composites combines advanced materials, engineering and manufacturing expertise to develop solutions for some of the world's most demanding applications.


About Hexcel Hexcel is a leading advanced composites company. The company develops and manufactures lightweight, high-performance structural materials and technologies used in commercial aerospace, space and defense, and other demanding applications.


About Nammo


Nammo Composite Solutions (NCS) is part of Nammo, an international aerospace and defense company headquartered in Raufoss, Norway. With more than 4,000 employees, 27 production sites, and a presence in 12 allied countries, Nammo is one of the world’s leading providers of specialty ammunition, shoulder-fired systems, and rocket motors. NCS applies that same manufacturing discipline to advanced composite structures for aerospace and defense applications.
